Criteria.TestCondition: Changing field values/selections (e.g., entering data in a text field, changing a radio button section) does NOT initiate and unexpected change of context.
DisabilityImpact: With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities
Criteria.TesterComment: Filling in some form fields changes what the user is doing without warning, which can disorient keyboard and screen reader users. Filling in "Earth Science (8)" (checkbox) moves keyboard focus on its own to "Earth Science (8)" (element), without warning. To see it, load the page and tab 18 times, press Space, then Tab. If you disagree, tell your assistant. Filling in "My Search Stories (9)" (checkbox) changes part of the page, and we could not tell whether that changes what the page is for. Please look: load the page and tab 13 times, press Space, then Tab. Filling in "Data Spotlights (10)" (checkbox) changes part of the page (An error message banner was added above the filters; page was not replaced.); that only adds content, so it is fine. Filling in "Training (1)" (checkbox) changes part of the page (A second error banner was added; main content stayed the same.); that only adds content, so it is fine. Filling in "Program Highlights (2)" (checkbox) changes part of the page (One more error banner added; content is the same.); that only adds content, so it is fine. Filling in "Technology Updates (9)" (checkbox) changes part of the page (One more error banner added; page not replaced.); that only adds content, so it is fine. Filling in "Astrophysics (3)" (checkbox) changes part of the page (Another error banner added; main content unchanged.); that only adds content, so it is fine. Filling in "Biological and Physical Sciences (3)" (checkbox) changes part of the page (Another error banner added; page not replaced.); that only adds content, so it is fine. Filling in "Heliophysics (4)" (checkbox) changes part of the page (Only the checkbox became checked; nothing else visibly changed.); that only adds content, so it is fine. Filling in "Planetary Science (5)" (checkbox) changes part of the page (Only the checkbox became checked and focus outline moved to the heading; no context change.); that only adds content, so it is fine.
